findings.finding: Volvo CE, Ferronordic's main supplier, reported Q3 2026 North America deliveries of 1,911 machines vs 1,352 (+41%) and net order intake of 1,960 vs 1,086 (+80%), an acceleration from about +9% in H1 (9M deliveries 5,245 vs 4,405), on data-centre, energy-infrastructure and onshoring demand. It published a week after ABG's preview, which assumed group sales of only +11% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 US-led revenue beat (+34% vs ABG) -> +23.2% (2026-08-12); Q1 2026 -> +13.6% (estimated-cadence history in baseline). This name has bought beats.
findings.why_not_priced: ABG's Q3e (2026-10-16) came before this counterparty data and has not been revised. FNM closed 86.2 on Volvo's report day (-0.5%) and is 91 now, below its 109 September high. If the read-through had been priced, the stock would have re-rated on 10-23 or ABG would have published an upgrade. Turnover is $122k/day with commissioned coverage only, so few people do this read-through. Caveat: these are Volvo's deliveries to all NA dealers, not Rudd's retail sales; part of the gain reverses Q3 2025 dealer destocking and part may be dealer inventory build. Sized as a proxy.
findings.independence: Ferronordic's own Q2 US commentary ('demand remained strong, supported by infrastructure activity and accelerating construction of data centers'), https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bdc7ac3ca2c70e411e3cc78b1f134f60b&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: The one sourced bar-setter has under-estimated badly: on Q2 2026 ABG had sales of SEK 1,159m and EBIT of SEK 41m against actuals of 1,558m (+34%) and 68m (+65%), a beat in all three segments. Its Q3e of 1,178m implies a 24% q/q drop.
findings.why_not_priced: A cautious bar from a single commissioned analyst is the bar the market reads, because nobody else publishes one. Part of the Q2 beat was German deliveries deferred from Q1, which do not recur, so ABG's normalisation is partly justified. Hence the small size: this is inference about estimate error, not a number.

findings.finding: German side: Volvo Trucks Europe Q3 orders +22% and European heavy-duty registrations +8% YTD (Volvo Q3), and Volvo/Renault German registrations +18% in Q3 with the toll-mileage index improving (ABG). Supportive for Ferronordic Germany's truck sales and aftermarket.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Germany swinging to profit (SEK 8m vs -13m) was part of the Q2 beat that moved +23.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: The German registration figure is already in ABG's preview, so it is inside the bar and sized near 0. Only the Volvo Europe order strength is new since the preview. Volvo also says German construction demand 'has yet to show a material improvement', but that is construction equipment, not Ferronordic's truck business there.

findings.finding: The Housby Heavy (Iowa) acquisition, closed 2026-02-03 (USD 26.6m 2024 CE revenue, about SEK 60m a quarter), adds inorganic US revenue absent from Q3 2025, and ABG expects margin uplift from moving Housby's overhead to Rudd's HQ.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: no separate reaction; the announcement (2026-01-06) came in a strong YTD run
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is public and presumably in ABG's model. Sized near 0 and kept only because it is a sourced fact bearing on the y/y comparison.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: the caveat did not stop the +23.2% on Q2
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: ABG's 'normalisation' Q3e reflects it. It is small because it is a company statement that lowers the reach of finding 1, not a number.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is roughly neutral (-0.16, run-up only, no short anchor). The stock is +3% over 20 days but well below its September high, so a positive lean does not just repeat the tape. The supplier read-through cuts mildly against the recent drawdown.
